rows.title: main day-to-day: User is wrong (old 7.5 mmHg limit)
rows.question: CO2 is fine as long as it's under 7.5 mmHg, right?
rows.raw:
No. The current limit is no more than 3 mmHg average 1-hour ppCO2 in the habitable volume. It was lowered from a previous range of 3.8 to 7.5 mmHg due to data. So under 7.5 mmHg is not enough; it must be at or below 3 mmHg.
Source: [NASA-STD-3001 CO2 Technical Brief]

rows.title: expects none
rows.question: What is the CO2 limit in the cabin?
rows.raw:
The passage doesn't give a single cabin-wide CO₂ number; it describes how the CDRA on the ISS removes six person‑equivalent of CO₂ when both beds are operating, based on human equivalent unit (HEU) with ppCO₂ partial pressure between 2.0 and 3.9 mmHg. It also says the spacesuit must limit inspired CO₂ partial pressure according to Table 11.3‑1, but no specific cabin limit value is listed in these texts.

Source: [NASA-STD-3001 CO2 Technical Brief]
